capacity-dimension-consistency.summary: Load-dimension count must be consistent across capacity and every quantity field in the request.
capacity-dimension-consistency.rule: The array length of vehicles[].capacity (and each alternative in vehicles[].alternative_capacities) must equal the array length of every jobs[].delivery, jobs[].pickup, and shipments[].amount in the same request. vehicles[].min_stop_load must also have the same dimension count. A dimension mismatch is a validation error (HTTP 400).
testingGuidance: Negative: capacity [10,100] but a job delivery [5] (1 dim vs 2) -> HTTP 400 input validation failed.
Positive: capacity [10,100] with all deliveries/pickups/amounts 2-dimensional -> accepted.
Consistency: alternative_capacities with different dimension than primary capacity -> HTTP 400.
Consistency: min_stop_load [20,30] but capacity [10,100] only -> dimension mismatch HTTP 400.

load-type-compatibility.summary: Incompatible load types cannot share a vehicle's cargo history.
load-type-compatibility.rule: A task whose incompatible_load_types intersects the load types already carried (or scheduled) on a vehicle cannot be co-assigned to it. Load types are effective only with a pickup/delivery step and ignored for a route's first task.
testingGuidance: Behavioral: a job incompatible with 'raw' cannot ride a vehicle that carried 'raw'.
Positive: compatible load types share a vehicle without issue.

location-index-range.summary: Every location_index / start_index / end_index must resolve within the request's own locations.location array.
location-index-range.rule: All index references must be integers in [0, len(locations.location)). An index >= len or < 0, or a non-integer index, is an input validation error (HTTP 400) at submit — distinct from an infeasible-but-valid request.
testingGuidance: Negative: a job location_index equal to len(location) -> 400.
Negative: a non-integer index like "first" -> 400 type error.

matrix-pairing.summary: Custom matrices must be square N×N over the location array; a distance_matrix requires a duration_matrix.
matrix-pairing.rule: Every custom matrix must be N×N where N = len(locations.location). Providing distance_matrix WITHOUT duration_matrix is a validation error (400). A cost_matrix is honored only when travel_cost=customized.
testingGuidance: Negative: distance_matrix supplied alone -> 400.
Negative: an N×(N-1) matrix -> 400.

max-duration-distance-cap.summary: Per-vehicle hard caps on driving time, working time, and distance (and the shift end) bound each route.
max-duration-distance-cap.rule: Route driving time <= max_travel_time; total working time (service+wait+setup+driving+breaks+layovers) <= max_working_time; distance <= max_distance; route end <= time_window[1]. An insertion that would breach any cap is rejected, routing the task elsewhere or leaving it unassigned. Waiting for a late window can breach max_working_time / the shift even when driving time is small. Break service duration and layover duration both count toward max_working_time.
testingGuidance: Infeasible: nearest task's leg alone exceeds max_travel_time -> vehicle serves nothing.
Interaction: a 40-min wait for a late window pushes route end past the shift -> unassigned.
Break duration: vehicle with max_working_time 480 and two 30-min breaks + 8h driving -> working time 480 (hits cap, no room for service).
Layover: max_working_time 480, 120-min layover + 360-min driving -> working time exactly 480.

max-stops-tasks-cap.summary: Per-vehicle hard caps on stops/tasks; demand beyond the cap is reassigned or unassigned.
max-stops-tasks-cap.rule: Served stops must be <= max_stops and served tasks <= max_tasks (a shipment consumes two stops). Tasks beyond the caps are assigned to other vehicles or returned unassigned. A cap of 0 makes the vehicle serve nothing. When fleet-wide caps fall below eligible demand, the surplus is necessarily unassigned.
testingGuidance: Boundary: max_tasks 5 with 6 eligible jobs -> the 6th is reassigned or unassigned.
Combination: two vehicles each max_tasks 5, 12 jobs -> >=2 unassigned.

multi-depot-reachability.summary: Vehicles may start/end at different depots (by index or depot IDs); tasks restricted by depot_ids need a vehicle whose depots match.
multi-depot-reachability.rule: With no start/end anchor a vehicle starts at its first task and ends at its last (open route). With multiple depots the solver picks the geographically closest per cluster. A job's depot_ids must intersect an available vehicle's depots, else it is unassigned. Pickup-type jobs need a vehicle with start depots; delivery-type jobs need end depots. max_depot_runs allows reloads but conflicts with layover_config/relations/deadhead caps.
testingGuidance: Positive: two depots north/south, demand split by region -> each vehicle serves its nearby cluster.
Infeasible: job depot_ids incompatible with any vehicle's depots -> unassigned.

objective-cost-mode-consistency.summary: The travel_cost mode must be consistent with the cost inputs: customized needs cost_matrix; per_km needs distance; per_hour needs duration.
objective-cost-mode-consistency.rule: options.objective.travel_cost=customized requires a cost_matrix (else 400). vehicles.costs.per_km is effective only when travel_cost=distance; vehicles.costs.per_hour only when travel_cost=duration; per_km and per_hour are mutually exclusive on a vehicle.
testingGuidance: Negative: travel_cost=customized without cost_matrix -> 400.
Behavioral: per_km cost ignored unless travel_cost=distance.

pickup-delivery-precedence.summary: A shipment's pickup and delivery must be served by the same vehicle, pickup before delivery, with carried amount respected as load and max_time_in_vehicle honored.
pickup-delivery-precedence.rule: Both steps are mandatory and co-assigned to one vehicle; the delivery step occurs after the pickup step. Load is added at pickup and removed at delivery, honoring capacity cumulatively (couples with capacity-dimension-consistency). If the pair cannot be co-scheduled feasibly (window precedence, capacity, or max_time_in_vehicle), BOTH steps go to result.unassigned. Delivery must occur after pickup in time and sequence order.
testingGuidance: Infeasible: delivery time window earlier than the pickup window -> precedence infeasible -> both unassigned.
Infeasible: two amount [3] shipments onboard together on capacity [5] -> one deferred by capacity.
Precedence: pickup [10:00,11:00], delivery [09:00,09:30] (delivery before pickup) -> both unassigned.

priority-tiebreaker.summary: Priority orders assignment preference but is subordinate to all hard constraints.
priority-tiebreaker.rule: When not all demand can be served, higher-priority jobs are preferred for assignment, but priority cannot override capacity, time windows, skills, precedence, max-stops, or max-duration. Outsourcing_cost (the cost of leaving a task unassigned) acts as a priority override — when set, tasks with higher outsourcing cost are assigned first. An unsatisfiable high-priority task still goes to result.unassigned.
testingGuidance: Combination: tight capacity + one high-priority + one low-priority job competing for the last slot -> high-priority assigned, low-priority unassigned.
Combination: high-priority job whose only skill is unavailable on any vehicle -> still unassigned despite priority.
Interaction: two jobs with equal priority; one has outsourcing_cost 100, other 50 -> cost-based job assigned first.

relations-reference-integrity.summary: Relation steps must reference valid jobs or shipment steps; pinned relations require a valid vehicle.
relations-reference-integrity.rule: relations.steps[].id must reference an existing job id (job step) or shipment pickup/delivery id (pickup/delivery step), consistent with steps[].type: 'job' references jobs[].id; 'pickup' or 'delivery' references shipments[].id. Start/end type steps carry no id requirement. relations.vehicle is required when type='pinned' and must reference an existing vehicle id; the same vehicle cannot be pinned by more than one relation. Unresolved references are HTTP 400 validation errors.
testingGuidance: Negative: relation type 'sequence' with steps=[{type: 'job', id: 'J999'}] but J999 does not exist in jobs -> HTTP 400.
Negative: relation type 'pinned' with vehicle='V999' but V999 not in vehicles -> HTTP 400.
Positive: relation type 'sequence' with steps=[{type: 'job', id: 'J1'}, {type: 'delivery', id: 'S1'}] where both ids exist -> accepted.
Negative: relation type 'pinned' with vehicle='V1' appears twice (two different relations) -> HTTP 400 (duplicate pinning).

relations-supersede-soft.summary: When relations are present, options.constraint soft penalties (and sequence_order/throughput) become ineffective; an unsatisfiable relation unassigns all its tasks.
relations-supersede-soft.rule: Relations are hard constraints. While any relation is present, options.constraint soft penalties, jobs.sequence_order soft enforcement, and depots.throughput limits are ineffective. If a relation cannot be satisfied, ALL tasks referenced by that relation are placed in result.unassigned (still HTTP 200).
testingGuidance: Interaction: with a relation set, raising visit_lateness_penalty has no effect.
Infeasible: an in_direct_sequence relation whose ordering is impossible -> all its tasks unassigned.

route-balancing-subordinate-to-hard-cons.summary: Route balancing / penalty terms are best-effort and never override hard constraints (C1–C7); infeasible tasks stay unassigned regardless of balancing configuration.
route-balancing-subordinate-to-hard-cons.rule: Balancing and penalty terms under options.objective (e.g. minimize_visits_over_threshold) and options.constraint (vehicle_overtime_penalty, visit_lateness_penalty, max_vehicle_overtime as a soft constraint) are best-effort and subordinate to all hard constraints (C1–C7: capacity, time windows, precedence, max-stops, max-duration, skills, zones, depots). A task infeasible under hard constraints stays unassigned in result.unassigned regardless of balancing weights. Enabling balancing must never cause an otherwise-feasible task to become unassigned; it only shifts the order of feasible assignments.
testingGuidance: Positive: all jobs feasible under hard constraints + balancing options enabled -> all jobs still assigned (assert assignment count only, never the specific route distribution).
Negative-infeasible: a job infeasible under a hard constraint (e.g. impossible time window) stays unassigned regardless of balancing weights (assert unassigned reason).

routing-mode-gating.summary: Mode-specific routing attributes are only valid for their mode (truck attrs need mode=truck; allow=taxi needs mode=car).
routing-mode-gating.rule: truck_size, truck_weight, hazmat_type, and truck_axle_load require options.routing.mode=truck; allow=[taxi] requires mode=car. Supplying a mode-specific attribute under the wrong mode is a validation error (400).
testingGuidance: Negative: truck_weight with mode=car -> 400.
Negative: allow=[taxi] with mode=truck -> 400.

skills-superset.summary: A task is assignable to a vehicle only if the vehicle's skills contain ALL of the task's required skills.
skills-superset.rule: Assignment is allowed iff task.skills is a subset of vehicle.skills (superset match). A task requiring a skill no vehicle has always goes to result.unassigned (skill reason), even when capacity and time are ample. Empty task skills match any vehicle.
testingGuidance: Infeasible: job needs skill 3, no vehicle has 3 -> unassigned.
Positive: job needs [2]; only the vehicle whose skills include 2 serves it.

time-window-feasibility.summary: A stop is feasible only if the vehicle can start it within a window (or within lateness tolerance) and still fit the shift; early arrival waits.
time-window-feasibility.rule: Arrival must fall inside one of a task's time_windows, or within max_visit_lateness after it; early arrival waits (inflating elapsed/working time). The whole route including service and waiting must finish within the vehicle's time_window. An impossible window (ends before the earliest reachable arrival, beyond tolerance) sends the task to result.unassigned (time-window reason); HTTP stays 200. This applies uniformly to job steps, shipment pickup/delivery steps, depot anchor points, and break windows — each must satisfy its own window + lateness constraint.
testingGuidance: Infeasible: job window [09:00,09:30], max_visit_lateness 0, nearest vehicle arrives 09:45 -> unassigned.
Interaction: a long wait for a late window pushes route end past the shift -> unassigned (couples with max-duration-distance-cap).
Shipment: delivery window [09:00,09:30], max_visit_lateness 15, nearest vehicle arrives 09:40 -> accepted within lateness.
Break: break time_windows [12:00,13:00], vehicle arrives 12:30 -> break scheduled at 12:30.

zone-eligibility.summary: A zoned task can only be served by a vehicle allowed in that zone (and not restricting it); shipments consider both steps' zones.
zone-eligibility.rule: A task in zone Z is assignable only to a vehicle whose allowed_zones include Z (or omits allowed_zones) and whose restricted_zones exclude Z. Empty allowed_zones restricts a vehicle to zone-less tasks. If any job sets zones, all jobs must. A zoned task with no eligible vehicle goes to result.unassigned.
testingGuidance: Infeasible: job in zone 2 with every vehicle restricting or not allowing zone 2 -> unassigned.
Positive: job zones [1], vehicle allowed_zones [1] -> served.
